Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx/429 and request for executive visibility

Locking down a few technical details so execs get a clear remediation timeline. Short version: we observed two correlated issues — a sudden shift in request size distribution (longer context windows) causing KV cache pressure and a client-side retry pattern that retriggered queued requests, producing backpressure and a cascade of 429s from the admission controller.

What were doing now (tech actions):
1) Apply tenant-level soft-rate limiter to break retry loops (temporary, non-persistent).
2) Route Acme traffic to the quantized model variant with lower resource per-token cost but compatible API — reduces latency by ~15% in our tests.
3) Increase mux slot pool + autoscaler margin for the serving fleet for the next 45 minutes.
4) Add a short-term circuit-breaker rule in the gateway to reject high-volume identical payloads per session.

Gaps identified:
- Alerts: There was no high-resolution 429 spike alert (we only had 5xx percent >5% aggregated over 15m). Need a 1m 429 spike alert and a retry-storm detector (ratio of retries to successes).
- Runbooks: No runbook documented for retry amplification scenarios; playbooks currently focus on model OOMs and GPU saturation.

ETA for initial mitigation (soft rate limit + routing) = ~25 mins from now. Full recovery (gateway rule + pool scale) = ~40 mins. Ill push logs to SUP-12345 and attach a short excerpt.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
